title: Rabbi Achai, a Fourth-Generation Palestinian Amora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Achai, a fourth-generation Palestinian Amora.

He is mentioned in [Terumot, beginning of chapter 10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.10.1.2): Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Achai transmit a teaching in Rabbi Ba bar Mamal’s name; and in Sanhedrin chapter 4, halakhah 7: Rabbi Hezekiah and Rabbi Achi transmit a teaching in Rabbi Abbahu’s name.

[Yalkut, Lekh Lekha](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Torah.76.8), on “What will You give me,” has Rabbi Achai and Rabbi Berekhya reporting Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani. [Yalkut, Kings I, remez 173](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.173.1), copies Rabbi Achi reporting Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Perhaps he is Rabbi Achi, who supervised bills of divorce in Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Assi’s time, as in [Gittin 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.5b.20). Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:8 has Rabbi Ba reporting Rabbi Achi; [Eruvin 9:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.9.2.2) has Rabbi Yose reporting Rabbi Achia. He is also mentioned in [Ketubot 3:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.3.4.4).[^2]

notes.text: Achai, Achi and Achia remain reported spellings. The identification with the supervisor of bills of divorce is tentative. The Shimon ben Gamliel abbreviation does not by itself specify a generation.

The linked Terumot and Lekh Lekha texts have Rav Acha where Hyman has Rabbi Achai. The linked Yalkut on Kings has Rabbi Achi with the abbreviation רשב״ן, whereas Hyman prints רשב״ג. In the linked Eruvin, the colleagues transmit the teaching in Rabbi Achiyah’s name before Rabbi Yose. In [the consulted Avodah Zarah parallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.2.8.13), Rabbi Ba transmits in Rav Attai’s name. Gittin names Rabbi Achi as the official over bills of divorce. Hyman’s proposed identification with that official remains tentative.
